answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, non-transferable bond in a vault before it may vote or claim rewards. The protocol releases the bond only after a delay, and slashes it when independent audits prove the identity double-counted work or colluded. Splitting influence across many identities therefore multiplies the capital at risk; laundering one bond through saffron-colored accounts or a prism of aliases does not create more voting weight. The attacker pays upfront, ties up funds, and risks losing them.
